case.description: Develop an analysis workflow to reconcile two synthetic reports of a batch transfer exercise. A reviewer must determine which discrepancies can be resolved from bounded records and which require a targeted follow-up request.
case.valued_outcome: For each of twelve batch identifiers, produce a reconciled quantity or explicit bounded disagreement, cite supporting records, and issue at most three follow-up requests that each name a missing field or record.
hard_constraints: Never silently drop duplicate or unmatched rows.
Use only the supplied unit-conversion table.
Do not infer missing quantities from neighboring batches.
Complete the review within sixty minutes.
resources: Two synthetic reports with thirty rows each, twelve batch identifiers, quantities, units and status fields.
Eight amendment records with explicit superseded-row references.
A table specifying that one fictional unit U equals five fictional units V, plus a status dictionary and report cutoff times.
Spreadsheet or local script environment and sixty minutes of reviewer time.
observations: Seven batches agree after applying the supplied conversion.
Three identifiers each occur twice in one report.

Awkward observation: the newer report includes an amendment whose effective time precedes both cutoffs, while the older report already includes its replacement quantity under a different row identifier.

openings.claim: Use a cutoff-aware row ledger with explicit replacement edges to separate quantity agreement from transaction-identity agreement.
openings.delta: Change the decision dependency from report recency to supported row lineage. Preserve every original row, duplicate and unmatched row with its batch, original quantity/unit, converted quantity, status interpretation and disposition. Apply only U=5V. Activate supersession only through explicit references and effective-time/cutoff checks. Equal quantities under different row identifiers are candidate correspondence, never proof of identity. Produce twelve batch results with citations: a definite quantity only when supported, otherwise a bounded disagreement without inferred missing quantities. Emit at most three requests naming missing fields or records, grouping affected identifiers where the same missing field applies; leave other uncertainty explicit.
openings.prediction: Against the nearest rival, taking the newer report as authoritative after conversion, the ledger should expose cases where a pre-cutoff amendment and an older replacement quantity would otherwise be counted inconsistently. In the disturbed copy, the missing superseded-row reference and undefined status should create explicit uncertainty instead of unsupported definite quantities. These are predictions, not supplied results.
openings.probe: Implement ledger and recency-rival variants in the supplied spreadsheet/script environment over the sixty rows, eight amendments and twelve identifiers. Run both on the supplied clean and disturbed copies within the shared sixty-minute review budget. Freeze outputs before opening the sealed key; use the extra twenty minutes for comparison of resolved-batch counts, unsupported definite claims and request counts. Also check complete row dispositions and record citations. Parsing/setup failure within the budget means the probe was infeasible, not successful.
assumptions: Explicit references and the supplied dictionary permit some unambiguous dispositions; no unstated cross-report identity mapping is assumed.
Capacity depends on implementing these bounded operations within sixty minutes; this is unverified.

Defeat the claimed advantage if the key shows no reduction in unsupported claims, incorrect lineage handling, or fewer justified resolutions without compensating accuracy. Reject operational suitability if time exceeds sixty minutes, requests exceed three, or any hard constraint fails.

openings.claim: Speculatively, a provenance ledger could recognize an already represented retroactive correction across changed row identifiers, preventing a second application while preserving every reported occurrence.
openings.delta: Change the reconciliation dependency from row-ID replacement alone to an evidence graph carried by immutable row occurrences, explicit supersession edges, status meanings and cutoff eligibility. Matching normalized quantities suggest candidate aliases but never establish identity. Nearest rival: literal superseded-row lookup with the same occurrence-preserving ledger.
openings.prediction: If explicit records uniquely establish cross-report representation, the graph should reconcile the awkward amendment without double application. The rival should retain a disagreement when literal identifiers cannot establish representation. Removing a needed supersession edge or introducing an undefined status should withdraw affected definite conclusions. If both variants behave identically, the proposed capability remains unconfirmed.
openings.probe: Within the sixty-minute review, use the local script or spreadsheet to run both variants on both supplied copies, reserving ten minutes to freeze twelve per-batch outputs and record citations. Retain duplicate and unmatched occurrences; normalize only U=5V; never impute neighboring quantities. Each output is a quantity or an explicit disagreement describing competing records and unknowns. Issue at most three prioritized requests, each naming a missing field or record; preserve remaining disagreements. During the separate twenty-minute comparison, open the sealed key and compare resolved-batch counts, unsupported definite claims and request counts. Examine whether the disturbed records specifically change justified conclusions. No distinguishing case makes the experiment inconclusive.
assumptions: The supplied records may lack authoritative links between differently identified replacement rows; quantity equality and chronology alone cannot supply them.
Defeat conditions: a claimed alias lacks explicit support, a definite quantity survives loss of indispensable evidence, or the sealed key contradicts it.

Capacity is unproved: if constructing and checking both variants cannot fit the review budget, freeze bounded disagreements. More than three independent gaps limits follow-up coverage without permitting invented resolution.
